title: Jordan at the World Cup
description: Jordan's World Cup debut in 2026 is the culmination of decades of development. How well do you know the Nashama?

questions.q: Jordan are making their World Cup debut in 2026. Which Asian championship final did they reach just before qualifying?
questions.explain: Jordan reached the final of the 2023 AFC Asian Cup — their best ever continental result — before losing to host nation Qatar 3–1. The run showed Jordan's emergence as a genuine Asian football power.

questions.q: Jordan's national team is nicknamed the Nashama. What does this word mean in Arabic?
questions.explain: Nashama means 'brave' or 'courageous' in Arabic — a fitting nickname for a team that has punched above their weight in Asian football and qualified for the World Cup for the first time.

questions.q: Mousa Al-Taamari is Jordan's most dynamic attacker. Which European league does he compete in?
questions.explain: Mousa Al-Taamari has played Ligue 1 football in France, bringing European experience to Jordan's national team. His pace and technique make him one of the most exciting players in Jordanian football history.

questions.q: Jordan qualified for the 2026 World Cup through the AFC qualifying process. How many AFC teams qualify automatically for the 2026 World Cup?
questions.explain: The AFC received 8 automatic World Cup places for 2026 — up from 4.5 in previous cycles. This expansion was key to Jordan qualifying, as it increased Asia's representation at the 50-year 48-team tournament.

questions.q: Jordan's football has developed rapidly under the patronage of the Royal family. Which member of the Royal family is heavily involved in Jordanian football development?
questions.explain: Prince Ali bin Al-Hussein has been a major figure in Jordanian and international football administration, serving on FIFA's executive committee and championing football development in Jordan.

questions.q: Jordan's home matches are played in Amman. What is the national stadium called?
questions.explain: King Abdullah II International Stadium in Amman is Jordan's national football venue, hosting home qualifiers and international matches. Its modern facilities reflect Jordan's investment in football infrastructure.

questions.q: In the 2023 AFC Asian Cup semi-final, Jordan beat which nation on the way to the final?
questions.explain: Jordan beat Japan in the 2023 AFC Asian Cup semi-final — one of the tournament's biggest shocks. Japan were one of Asia's elite nations; Jordan's win showed their rise to a new level in Asian football.

questions.q: Jordan's 2026 World Cup qualification ended how many years without a World Cup appearance for the country?
options: Jordan has never appeared at a World Cup before 2026
questions.explain: 2026 is Jordan's first ever World Cup appearance. They have come close to qualifying before — including an intercontinental play-off defeat to Uruguay in 2013 — but 2026 marks their historic debut.

questions.q: Jordan's Baha' Faisal scored a memorable goal in the 2023 Asian Cup — what type of goal was it that went viral?
options: A half-way line lob over the goalkeeper
A solo dribble from his own half
questions.explain: Baha' Faisal's stunning lob from near the halfway line — spotting the goalkeeper off his line — went viral and became one of Asian football's most memorable goals of recent years, showcasing Jordan's increasing quality.

questions.q: Which confederation does Jordan belong to?
questions.explain: Jordan are members of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC). Their qualification through Asian qualifying for 2026 is a landmark achievement for the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.
